 Kmart expands beauty offering with 2,700 products and 117 global brands 
 by 
 Michelle Ruzzene 
 November 6, 2026 November 6, 2026 
  
 Kmart has significantly expanded its beauty category, introducing more than 2,700 products from over 117 global brands, including some of the biggest names in K-Beauty. With more than 60 per cent of the range exclusive to Kmart and Target in Australia, the expansion signals the retailer’s growing ambitions in the competitive beauty market. 
 Australian beauty retail is becoming increasingly competitive, with Kmart making a major play for market share through an expanded beauty offering featuring thousands of skincare, make-up and fragrance products.
 The discount department store has introduced more than 2,700 beauty products from over 117 global brands, with more than 60 per cent of the range exclusive to Kmart and Target in Australia.
 The expansion represents a significant step beyond Kmart’s established OXX Cosmetics private-label range, bringing internationally recognised beauty brands to its value-conscious customer base.
 Global beauty brands take centre stage
 Among the brands joining Kmart’s expanded beauty portfolio are Korean skincare favourites Medicube, Biodance, Abib and SKIN1004, alongside make-up brands SHEGLAM and Daise.
 The retailer is also introducing international names including Troublemaker, BRINGGREEN, Tree Hut, Tony Moly and Essence.
 Glow Hub and Colorgram are among the brands being introduced to Australian shoppers through Kmart and Target’s nationwide retail network.
 Nicola Farrell, Business Manager – Beauty at Kmart, said the expansion reflects strong customer demand for greater variety and affordability.
 “We’re invested in giving shoppers choice and value when it comes to beauty, and are delighted to be bringing some amazing international brands like Glow Hub and Colorgram to Aussie shores as a nationwide stockist across Kmart and Target stores, with 60% of beauty products available exclusively to our customers. We are seeing huge demand for the beauty category from our shoppers and are delighted to bring them even more options to level up their skincare routine or add a little fun to their make-up bag.” 
 K-Beauty drives category growth
 Korean beauty is a major focus of the expanded assortment, reflecting growing Australian consumer interest in innovative skincare formulations, ingredients and multi-step routines.
According to data from Future Market Insights, cited by ABC News and highlighted by Kmart, Australia ranks second globally for per-capita spending on Korean beauty products, behind only South Korea, highlighting the growing appetite for K-Beauty among Australian consumers.
 The retailer is capitalising on this demand by introducing brands including Arencia, Abib, The Face Shop and Beauty of Joseon.
 The move also reflects the increasing mainstream accessibility of K-Beauty, with products once primarily associated with specialist beauty retailers and online platforms becoming available through mass-market retail channels.
 For beauty brands and distributors, Kmart’s expansion highlights the growing importance of accessible price points, international trends and exclusive product assortments in attracting Australian shoppers.
 OXX Cosmetics expands its affordable beauty range
 Alongside its growing portfolio of international brands, Kmart is continuing to invest in its own OXX Cosmetics range, introducing new products across colour cosmetics, skincare and fragrance.
 New additions include:
 3 Piece Lip Kits: $10
 Eyeshadow Cream Sticks: $6
 Blur and Gloss Lip Stains: $8
 Korean-made OXX Sheet Face Masks: From $2
 OXX Eau de Parfum: From $6
 What Kmart’s beauty expansion means for Australian retail
 Kmart’s investment in beauty signals the increasing importance of the category within Australia’s discount department store sector.
 By combining established international brands, trending Korean skincare and affordable private-label products, the retailer is positioning itself to compete for beauty spending across multiple consumer segments.
 The emphasis on exclusivity is particularly significant, providing Kmart and Target with a point of difference while giving international beauty brands access to an established national retail network.
 For the wider beauty industry, the expansion illustrates how mass-market retailers are responding to changing consumer expectations, with shoppers increasingly seeking trending products, recognised brands and value in the same retail destination.
